Changes in age-adjusted death rates* with COVID-19 as underlying cause, by race/ethnicity
From 2020 to 2021, disparities in AADR ratios from COVID-19 decreased significantly by 14.0%–40.2% for most racial and ethnic groups
This analysis used U.S. provisional mortality data from death certificates collected by CDC’s National Vital Statistics System

methods_quotes.q: Z-tests of statistical significance were used to compare differences in the percent change in each measure of relative disparity.
Pearson’s chi-square tests of differences in the distribution of decedents by sex, age group, and race and ethnicity
Crude death rates were calculated by sex, age group, and race and ethnicity, and AADRs were calculated by race and ethnicity.
Using the non-Hispanic multiracial group (the group with the lowest death rate) as the referent group
To assess sensitivity of the results to changing the referent group, separate analyses were conducted with multiracial and non-Hispanic White persons as referent groups.
P-values <0.05 were considered statistically significant (Pearson’s chi-square).
